conflicts.point: Whether the Bureau of Industry and Security enforcement mechanisms under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 effectively contain dual-use proliferation or merely function as cartel maintenance for major cloud providers.

positions.stance: Export controls and administrative choke points successfully limit the spread of dangerous model weights and prevent irreversible distribution.
Export controls fail to stop bad actors while imposing prohibitive compliance costs that eliminate small competitors and entrench cloud oligopolies.

conflicts.point: Whether public model weight releases are permanent deployments that permanently sever upstream control, or whether post-deployment telemetry and open-source peer review mitigate risks faster than central pre-screening.

positions.stance: Once model weights circulate on peer-to-peer networks, central remediation becomes impossible, making pre-market bans essential.
Decentralized telemetry and open peer review patch vulnerabilities faster and more effectively than centralized regulatory gatekeeping.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the Bureau of Industry and Security enforcement mechanisms under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 effectively contain dual-use proliferation or merely function as cartel maintenance for major cloud providers.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position succeeds because it evaluates both the intended security outcome and the observable market distortion caused by licensing overhead. The safetyist claim relies on statutory authority without demonstrating actual containment efficacy against determined actors who bypass trade controls.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical evidence showing that export controls successfully block illicit model proliferation without imposing prohibitive compliance costs on small developers would tilt the balance toward the safetyist claim.

verdicts.conflict: Whether public model weight releases are permanent deployments that permanently sever upstream control, or whether post-deployment telemetry and open-source peer review mitigate risks faster than central pre-screening.
verdicts.rationale: This empirical dispute remains undecidable because both decentralized peer review and unauthorized proliferation are dynamic phenomena lacking long-term quantitative baselines. Both sides project theoretical risk models without sufficient empirical testing from actual open-source frontier releases.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Systematic post-release tracking data from past open-weight model deployments that quantifies both malicious exploitation rates and community-led remediation speeds would resolve this conflict.
